content:
Earlier than June, we have already named three Russian banks sanctioned by the US, whose client applications have successfully smuggled onto the App Store. Two months later, another similar example has climbed to the top of the iPhone App Store.

"K8CHEN PRO" is the latest example. Its App Store listing page is disguised as a kitchen design application using augmented reality (AR).

As soon as you open the app, the disguise quickly falls apart. The privacy policy linked in the App Store claims to be generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator", which itself may be a red flag.

In short, this app is 100% the client app of T-Bank (Tinkoff Bank). What interests me the most is that such apps have repeatedly passed Apple App Store's review mechanism.

When they appear on the App Store charts due to widespread coverage, they look so blatantly obvious that even a fool can see these should never have been listed. The situation is indeed puzzling.

The reports about the two from June can be seen here and here.

Update: As expected, the app has been removed from the App Store.

Make the most of your Apple products
